depicted_event_note: Not an event photograph. It shows a museum display of a Teletype Model 33 ASR, photographed in 2014. The unit's manufacture date is not stated at the source. It is not Dartmouth's equipment.

depicted_subject.model: Model 33 ASR (ASR-33) teleprinter with integrated paper-tape reader/punch
depicted_subject.location_when_photographed: Computer History Museum, Mountain View, California (per photographer's description)
depicted_subject.unit_history: Unknown. A decal reading 'TimeShare Corporation' is on the platen cover; no source explains it.

evidence: CHM Revolution gallery artifact page for the ASR-33 states 'Date Introduced: 1964' (https://www.computerhistory.org/revolution/minicomputers/11/337/1934, read 2026-09-15).
Secondary sources (Wikipedia 'Teletype Model 33', seen via search summary only) give 1963. Not independently verified.
model_introduction_date.resolution: Conflicting 1963/1964. Leave the year out of any caption, or say 'early 1960s'.

relationship_to_script_claim.classification: representative period hardware, not the Dartmouth unit
evidence: Dartmouth Computation Center, 'The Dartmouth Time-Sharing System: A Brief Description', 19 Oct 1964: consoles are 'model 35 teletype machines' (text, p.1; schematic, p.2).
GE Computer Dept. Laboratory revision of the same, 26 Mar 1965: 'model 33/35 teletype machines'.
relationship_to_script_claim.limit: The Model 33 is documented for the Dartmouth system only from GE's March 1965 revision. Dartmouth's own October 1964 text names Model 35. Do not caption this image as the terminal BASIC first ran on, or as Dartmouth hardware.

version_model_evidence: Photographer's Commons description names the Teletype Corporation ASR-33.
Museum card at the right edge of the frame is headed 'ASR-33 Telet…' (cut off by the photo edge, soft focus). Its visible opening words match the CHM Revolution label for the ASR-33.
Integrated paper-tape punch/reader at left with START/STOP/FREE switch, the 'A' (automatic send-receive) configuration.
Model 33 keyboard layout, with visible CTRL, ESC and SHIFT keycaps.
